A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FaceCoT dataset and CEPL framework despite the changed title and formatting. Their complete main texts, appendices, tables, equations, and figures support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original cross-dataset FAS results, training and resolution ablations, caption-model annotation accuracy, and qualitative model outputs.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds leave-one-domain-out comparisons, attack-type analysis, and zero-shot versus fine-tuned backbone evaluations.

M1.justification: The six-part annotation format, accuracy/format rewards, and two-stage CEPL procedure remain unchanged, including encoder transfer, resetting other components, and LoRA adaptation. Additional backbone tests and newly documented confidence scoring do not establish a revised method.

E1.justification: FaceCoT retains the same source datasets, sample composition, and 14 attack types, and evaluation covers the same 11 benchmark domains. The added OULU/CASIA/Replay/MSU experiments change training and testing roles within existing coverage rather than introducing a new domain or task.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains its comparator set. New Table 7 adds comparisons with FGHV, GDA, PatchNet, SSAN, IADG, UDG-FAS, TTDG, SA-FAS, DIVT-M, GAC-FAS, and CFPL, alongside FLIP and I-FAS. Table 9 additionally evaluates zero-shot MiniCPMV and Qwen2.5-VL baselines.

E3.justification: The added experiments introduce four leave-one-domain-out training/testing configurations using caption-annotated benchmark training splits. They also introduce zero-shot controls and a Qwen2.5-VL-7B configuration alongside MiniCPMV-2.6-8B. The original 11-dataset protocol and stated training hyperparameters remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds a seven-attack Rose-Youtu breakdown, backbone-dependent zero-shot/fine-tuning analysis, a reported manual audit of 5,000 Silver annotations, and a real-face explanation case. Existing CEPL, RL, and resolution ablations remain; v1 Tables 7–8 become v2 Tables 10–11.

E5.justification: Section 5.1 newly states that all experiments use three random seeds and report averaged results. This discloses repeated-run practice without establishing an increase in runs. Neither version reports corresponding dispersion estimates, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: New Tables 7–9 substantially expand reported results: leave-one-domain-out averages are 1.06% HTER and 99.85% AUC, while Qwen2.5-VL changes from 19.60%/83.75% zero-shot to 9.32%/95.72% after training. Attack-specific outcomes and a real-face example are also added. All 192 numerical entries in Table 1 and the retained ablation results are unchanged.

T1.justification: No theoretical assumptions, propositions, proofs, or derivations are added or revised. The accuracy formula is retained. New Equation 2 documents standard two-token softmax confidence computation for the existing evaluation, rather than introducing a new mathematical result.

C1.justification: The introduction corrects the swapped headline improvements from 5.00 AUC points and 4.06 HTER points to 4.06 AUC points and 5.00 HTER points, matching unchanged Table 1. The central contributions—FaceCoT, its RL-assisted expansion, and CEPL—retain their meaning and scope.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations concerning protocol saturation, backbone transferability, attack-type bias, and positive authenticity cues for real faces. It acknowledges that FaceCoT's use as an evaluation benchmark remains underexplored and substantially expands fairness/privacy discussion. The new assertion of no observable demographic subgroup bias lacks a quantitative subgroup comparison.

D1.justification: The supplement newly explains beam count, first-token Yes/No logits, and confidence computation for AUC/HTER. It discloses annotation costs, caption-model training and annotation compute, and six annotators working for three days. It also clarifies the intended annotation-only release and source-license documentation. These are disclosures, not demonstrated changes to existing experiments.

R1.justification: The FAS references are refreshed with works such as S-Adapter and content-aware composite prompt engineering, plus references supporting the added comparisons; several older references are removed. The GPT-4o system-card reference is replaced by the GPT-4 technical report. The overarching FAS/CoT positioning and novelty claims remain essentially unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 retitles the paper, makes localized prose corrections and expansions, and reorganizes lettered appendices into numbered supplementary sections. Most main-text paragraphs and the central narrative sequence remain closely matched; the added scientific material does not constitute a wholesale rewrite.

P2.justification: The document switches from single-column to two-column formatting, with widespread resizing, relocation, and restyling of figures and tables. v2 adds Tables 7–9 and a real-face panel in Figure 11, and rearranges Figure 10's examples from five columns to three. Retained appendix tables are renumbered rather than replaced.

improvement.justification: The added protocol and backbone comparisons usefully extend v1's already broad evaluation. Confidence-score documentation, resource disclosures, and corrected headline figures improve reproducibility and accuracy. These gains are tempered by unquantified fairness assurances and seed averaging without dispersion estimates. The revision provides useful additional support while leaving the central method and original benchmark findings unchanged.
